items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f, and it runs straight into त with no vowel between: haftaa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: हफ़्ता is a week. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so the gender is predictable and the plural becomes हफ़्ते. The word came from Persian and carries the dotted फ़ pronounced as an f, joined to त in a stack. The Sanskrit-derived सप्ताह means the same thing and appears in formal writing.

examples.note: पूरा takes -ा because हफ़्ता is masculine.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
Both masculine, and both ending in -ा.

practice.question: हफ़्ता
practice.explanation_en: हफ़्ता is a week. The formal word सप्ताह means the same.

game.question_en: राम ___ हफ़्ता — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: हफ़्ता is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy घ, and the dot before ट is read as the retroflex nasal: ghaṇṭaa.

learn.explanation_en: घंटा is an hour, and also a bell — the two senses are related, since bells marked the hours. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so both the gender and the plural are predictable. The anusvara sits before ट, a retroflex, so it is read with the tongue curled back.

examples.note: The singular, used for a single hour.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
पूरा takes -ा to agree.

practice.question: घंटा
practice.explanation_en: घंटा is an hour. The same word also means a bell.

game.question_en: राम ___ घंटा — का, के or की?

items.pronunciation_notes: The final vowel drops, giving samay in two syllables rather than three.

learn.explanation_en: समय is time in the general sense — the thing you have too little of, rather than a reading on a clock. It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable, and the plural does not change. You met the word in Module 2 as an example of य closing a word.

examples.note: अच्छा takes -ा because समय is masculine.
कम never changes form.
The masculine adjective ending again.

practice.question: समय
practice.explanation_en: समय is time in general. घड़ी is the clock or watch that measures it.

game.question_en: राम ___ समय — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: समय is masculine, so का. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

summary.recap_en: This level added हफ़्ता, घंटा and समय. The first two end in -ा and announce their gender; समय ends in a consonant and does not.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last time word, and the question words that close the module.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ख़ is a scraping sound at the back of the mouth, though many speakers say a plain ख: taariiḳh.

learn.explanation_en: तारीख़ is a calendar date. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. The word came from Arabic through Persian and carries the dotted ख़, which you met in Module 2 — most speakers pronounce it as a plain ख, and that is perfectly normal.

examples.note: नया takes its irregular feminine नई here.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
पुराना takes -ी to agree.

game.question_en: राम ___ तारीख़ — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: तारीख़ is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending predicts nothing.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्य stack runs क straight into य with no vowel between: kyaa, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: क्या asks about things rather than people — for a person you need कौन. It is not a noun, so it carries no gender of its own. It has a second job you will meet in Module 5: placed at the front of a statement it turns the whole thing into a yes-or-no question, rather like a spoken question mark.

examples.note: Asking about an object.
The start of the commonest question there is.
Said on its own, this is an exclamation of admiration.

practice.question: क्या
practice.explanation_en: क्या is what. कौन is who.

game.question_en: The answer is किताब. Which question word fits?
game.explanation_en: किताब is a thing, not a person, so the question takes क्या rather than कौन.

items.pronunciation_notes: The open औ is a single vowel nearer the aw of 'law' than the ow of 'cow': kaun.

learn.explanation_en: कौन asks about people, where क्या asks about things. Keeping the two apart is the first thing to get right about Hindi questions, since English speakers reaching for 'what' will sometimes need कौन instead. You met the word in Module 1 as an example of the open औ.

examples.note: Asking about a person.
The same pattern with another person.
Two question words joined.

practice.question: कौन
practice.explanation_en: कौन is who. क्या is what.

game.question_en: The answer is राम. Which question word fits?
game.explanation_en: राम is a person, so the question takes कौन rather than क्या.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the ten time words with तारीख़ and opened the question words. क्या asks about things and कौन about people — the distinction English blurs and Hindi keeps.
summary.next_up_en: Next: कहाँ, कब and कैसे — place, time and manner.

items.pronunciation_notes: The crescent nasalises the final vowel and adds no n sound: kahãa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: कहाँ asks about place. It pairs with यहाँ, meaning here, and वहाँ, meaning there — all three end in the same nasalised vowel, which makes them easy to learn as a set. The crescent nasalises the vowel without adding any n sound of its own.

examples.note: The question word comes before the verb.
The same pattern with another verb.
Two question words joined.

practice.question: कहाँ
practice.explanation_en: कहाँ is where. यहाँ is here and वहाँ is there.

game.question_en: The answer is घर. Which question word fits?
game.explanation_en: घर is a place, so the question takes कहाँ.

items.pronunciation_notes: Unaspirated क with no puff of air, and the final vowel drops: kab, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: कब asks about time. It is the shortest of the question words and the easiest to say, but keep the opening क free of breath — with a puff it drifts towards ख. Expect the answer to be one of the time words from the last few levels: सुबह, शाम, कल or a date.

examples.note: The question word comes before the verb.
The same pattern with the opposite verb.
The pair reversed from the last card.

practice.question: कब
practice.explanation_en: कब is when. कहाँ is where.

game.question_en: The answer is सुबह. Which question word fits?
game.explanation_en: सुबह is a time, so the question takes कब.

items.pronunciation_notes: The open ऐ then a flat ए, with no glide on either: kaise, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: कैसे asks about manner — how something is done. There is a related word कैसा, which asks what something is like and does change form, but कैसे itself is fixed when it means how. You met the word in Module 1 as an example of two flat vowels in one word, neither of them gliding.

examples.note: The question word comes before the verb.
A very useful question in a kitchen.
Two question words joined.

practice.question: कैसे
practice.explanation_en: कैसे is how, in the sense of by what means.

game.question_en: The answer is धीरे. Which question word fits?
game.explanation_en: धीरे describes the manner of doing something, so the question takes कैसे.

summary.recap_en: This level covered कहाँ, कब and कैसे — place, time and manner. Each expects a different kind of answer, and matching the question to the answer is what the game drills.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्य stack runs क into य, and the dot nasalises the vowel: kyoṁ, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: क्यों asks for a reason. It packs a stack and a nasalised vowel into a single syllable, which makes it the hardest of the question words to say cleanly — run the क straight into the य with no vowel between them, then let the vowel hum through the nose. क्यों नहीं, meaning 'why not', is worth learning as a phrase.

examples.note: The question word comes before the verb.
A ready-made phrase, used exactly as in English.
The pair reversed from the last level.

practice.question: क्यों
practice.explanation_en: क्यों is why. कैसे is how.

game.question_en: Which question word asks for a reason rather than a time or a place?
game.explanation_en: क्यों asks why. कब asks when, कहाँ asks where and कैसे asks how.

items.pronunciation_notes: The open औ is a single vowel, and the final vowel drops: aur, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: और joins two things, exactly as English 'and' does, and it has appeared in example phrases throughout this module. It also means 'more' — और चाय is more tea. You met it in Module 1 as one of the first words containing the open औ.

examples.note: Joining two nouns of opposite gender.
The same pattern with two drinks.
And with two people.

practice.question: और
practice.explanation_en: और is and. It also means 'more' when placed before a noun.

game.question_en: Which word joins two nouns together?
game.explanation_en: और joins two things. नहीं negates, हाँ agrees and बहुत quantifies.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot nasalises the long final vowel, so no separate n is heard at the end: nahiiṁ.

learn.explanation_en: नहीं does two jobs: it answers a question with 'no', and it negates a statement. It is the commonest negative in the language, and Module 5 will add न and मत, which negate in different situations. The dot nasalises the final vowel rather than adding a consonant, so the word ends with a hum and not with an n.

examples.note: Negating a verb.
The pair, joined by और.
The ready-made phrase from the first card of this level.

practice.question: नहीं
practice.explanation_en: नहीं is 'no' as an answer and 'not' inside a sentence.

game.question_en: Which word makes a statement negative?
game.explanation_en: नहीं negates. हाँ agrees, और joins and बहुत quantifies.

summary.recap_en: This level added क्यों, और and नहीं. क्यों completes the six question words, while और and नहीं are the two function words you will use in almost every conversation.
summary.next_up_en: Next: हाँ, बहुत and बात close the module.

items.pronunciation_notes: The crescent nasalises the vowel and adds no n: hãa, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: हाँ is yes, the counterpart of नहीं. Doubling it, हाँ हाँ, is very common and signals enthusiastic agreement rather than impatience. In more formal situations जी or जी हाँ is used instead, since जी on its own carries respect. The crescent nasalises the vowel with no n sounded.

examples.note: The pair again, from the other side.
Doubled for enthusiastic agreement.

practice.question: हाँ
practice.explanation_en: हाँ is yes. नहीं is no.

game.question_en: Which word agrees with what has just been said?
game.explanation_en: हाँ agrees. नहीं is its opposite, और joins and बहुत quantifies.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final vowel drops, giving bahut in two syllables rather than three.

learn.explanation_en: बहुत does the work of both 'very' and 'a lot'. Before an adjective it intensifies — बहुत अच्छा is very good — and before a noun it means a large quantity. It never changes form, whatever it modifies. Its opposite for quantity is कम, meaning little or less, which you have seen in examples.

examples.note: Intensifying an adjective.
The same pattern with another adjective.
Before a noun it means quantity instead.

practice.question: बहुत
practice.explanation_en: बहुत is very before an adjective, and a lot before a noun. कम is its opposite.

game.question_en: Which word means a large amount?
game.explanation_en: बहुत means a lot. कम is its opposite, meaning little or less.

items.pronunciation_notes: A dental त with the tongue on the teeth, and the final vowel drops: baat, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: बात is one of the hardest Hindi words to translate: it covers a remark, a topic, a matter, a point being made. बात करना is to talk, and क्या बात है can mean anything from 'what's the matter?' to 'how wonderful'. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable — and since the word appears constantly, this is one flag worth memorising outright.

examples.note: अच्छा takes -ी because बात is feminine.
The thing said comes before the verb.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.

common_error.why_en: बात is feminine despite its consonant ending, so the adjective takes -ी.

practice.question: बात
practice.explanation_en: बात is a thing said or a matter under discussion. शब्द is a single word.

game.question_en: राम ___ बात — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: बात is feminine, so की. Nothing in its shape says so, which is why it is flagged.

summary.recap_en: This level closed Module 4 with हाँ, बहुत and बात. Across 150 words the lesson has been consistent: every noun carries a gender, most endings do not reveal it, and the ones that seem to — like the -ी of पानी or the -ा of चिड़िया — sometimes point the wrong way.
summary.next_up_en: Module 5 turns these words into sentences, starting with होना and the pronouns.
